comparison: Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the organoid development and characterization (C1-C4, C20-C25). OpenEval emphasizes systematic testing and quantitative measurements, while peer reviewers highlight the novelty and ease of establishment. Peer reviewers also include C62-C63 (organoid utility) in this evaluation, which OpenEval addresses separately in R10.

Perfect agreement on claims C26-C37. Both evaluations support the immunostaining evidence for cell type identification and spatial organization. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of temporal progression and functional validation, while peer reviewers accept the findings without challenge and note the stereotypical arrangement allows identification without antibody staining.

Complete agreement on claims C5, C38-C42, C64. Both evaluations support the Ca2+ imaging data demonstrating coordinated dynamics. OpenEval emphasizes the quantitative robustness (104 peaks across 14 organoids), while peer reviewers explicitly accept the temporal relationship and synchronization findings without question.

Full agreement on claims C6, C43-C46, C66-C67. Both support the gap junction pharmacology findings. OpenEval notes a discrepancy requiring further investigation (CBX vs 18β-GA effects), while peer reviewers accept the nuanced finding that gap junctions affect ICC-to-SMC signaling but not overall rhythm without raising concerns.

Divergent evaluations on claims C7, C47-C50, C75. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to alternative mechanisms not being ruled out and speculative interpretation of mechanical feedback. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED and explicitly endorse this as a novel, convincing finding of SMC-to-ICC feedback, treating it as a key contribution.

Both support claims C51-C52, C76. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes assumptions about Nifedipine specificity and potential off-target effects not fully excluded. Peer reviewers accept the findings as complementary evidence for mechanical feedback hypothesis without raising specificity concerns.

Agreement on claims C8, C53-C56, C85-C87. Both support the organoid fusion findings. OpenEval notes the 'pause' phenomenon lacks mechanistic explanation and ICC rhythm adjustment interpretation is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers accept the observations without challenge, treating mechanistic speculation as reasonable interpretation.

Strong agreement on claims C57-C61, C88-C90. Both support the hydrogel system findings showing SMC-mediated synchronization. OpenEval notes the exact mechanism remains unclear and requires further investigation. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse this as convincing evidence for a novel, previously unappreciated role of SMCs.

Divergent evaluations on claims C81-C84. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting ICC subtype identification relies on morphology rather than specific markers and the proposed signaling sequence is speculative with lacking direct demonstration. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the interpretation as reasonable based on established morphological criteria.

Both support claims C62-C63 regarding organoid utility. OpenEval addresses these claims separately as a valid interpretation of the model's characteristics. Peer reviewers include these claims within their broader evaluation of organoid development (R1), accepting the simplified composition as a feature of the system.

Both support claim C65 (literature comparison). OpenEval notes the difference in latency times is not fully explained and could reflect multiple factors. Peer reviewers include this with background knowledge (C9-C19) and treat all literature citations as accepted context without questioning.

Complete agreement on claims C68-C72. Both support the discussion of literature controversies and proposed hypothesis. OpenEval notes the temporal model remains speculative and requires direct testing. Peer reviewers accept the interpretation as reasonable speculation supported by experimental data and analogous systems.

Both support claims C73-C74 regarding ICC structural properties. OpenEval treats these as established knowledge providing context for interpreting experimental results. Peer reviewers group these with speculative mechanism claims (C77-C80) and accept the structural basis for ICC non-contractility without challenge.

Divergent evaluations on claims C77-C80. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the conceptual framework is interesting but speculation about SMC-to-ICC feedback remains unproven and connection to previous work is indirect. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, treating the interpretive discussion and parallel to neural circuits as reasonable interpretation.

Complete agreement on claims C9-C19 (background knowledge). Both evaluations support these literature citations as accurate and providing necessary context. OpenEval addresses these separately from C65, while peer reviewers group all background claims together. Both treat these as established, uncontroversial context.
